findings.text: The dialect/backend guard covers only a store written before the columns: test_a_store_written_before_the_scalars_backfills_them builds an old `pointers` table and asserts the backfilled row folds as codex, but nothing asserts the dialect of a row written by the new `_write_pointer_row` (reckon/crew/station_store.py:724-730). Dropping `backend`/`dialect` from that INSERT leaves all four tests green, because log_path is still written (so the fixture's streams are still found) and the only codex pointer in the fixture is the one the pre-existing table carries; every newly ingested codex or other non-default run would then fold in the default dialect with no test reddening.

This 232-line figure script and the two SVGs beside it are outside the paths the node was declared: the dispatch and plan name reckon/crew/station_store.py, reckon/crew/recovery_stream.py, reckon/crew/review_records.py, tests/test_a_tick_decodes_only_what_changed.py and 'the node's fragment'. The census arm's 'at most 600 MB per tick' clause cannot discriminate: the base arm peaks at 175.5-251.0 MB (census/decode-census-base.log:2622, :2670, :2718, :2766, :2814, :2862) against the head's 185.6-244.6 MB, so a node that changed nothing would pass it and the head envelope is not lower than base's. The node's real discriminating evidence is the new test file (3 of 4 ids fail at base) and the disappearance of `_pointer_for_stream` from the head census, not the ceiling; the fragment reports the peaks honestly rather than claiming a fall, but the done_when clause it satisfies measures nothing about this change.
